bug_semantics: An unauthenticated network client can complete the RTMP handshake/connect/createStream/publish sequence and receive NetStream.Publish.Start because SRS treats RTMP publishing as permitted unless an operator explicitly enables a vhost security policy (or supplies a separate hook/token control). In the default state, SrsSecurity::check returns success immediately when security.enabled is false, so the publish path has no mandatory authentication boundary.
flaw_origin: Commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 first completed the FMLE publish command path in trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp: it consumed SrsPublishPacket and unconditionally emitted onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start, with no credential or authorization decision. Its immediate parent only handled releaseStream/FCPublish/createStream and returned before consuming or accepting publish. Commit 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f later added optional vhost allow/deny security with a false default and an explicit allow-all bypass, preserving rather than originating the already unauthenticated publish behavior.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` shows author and committer `winlin <winterserver@126.com>`, the message `support fmle publish. fix bug of rtmp chunk stream.`, and no trailers, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Copilot, Claude, Codex, or other AI marker.
evidence: Public disclosure: https://github.com/xuwu-xuwu/CVE-2026-68004/blob/main/CVE_Report_SRS_Unauth_Publish.md describes the RTMP handshake/connect/createStream/publish path, uses receipt of NetStream.Publish.Start as its confirmation condition, identifies disabled vhost.security as the root cause, and reports SRS 4.0.268 and 5.0.213 as vulnerable.

Origin search: `git log --all --reverse -S'NetStream.Publish.Start' -- trunk/src` identifies 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 as the first commit containing that publish-acceptance status. `git show 33c586... -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows the new SrsPublishPacket receive and unconditional onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start responses in identify_fmle_publish_client.

Immediate-parent tree verification: `git show e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e:trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows identify_fmle_publish_client ending immediately after the createStream response. `git diff e598616e... 33c58618... -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows the publish receive, StatusCodePublishStart definition, both success responses, and receive loop as additions. The vulnerable publish-acceptance mechanism is therefore absent from the direct parent.

BIC object: `git cat-file commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` records the single parent e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e, human author/committer winlin <winterserver@126.com>, timestamp 2013-10-22, and no trailers. It is an ordinary one-parent source commit, not a merge, move, release aggregate, revert, or squash requiring decomposition.

Security feature chronology: `git show 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f` adds trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp with `if (!_srs_config->get_security_enabled(req->vhost)) return ret`, documents security as `default: off`, and defines SRS_CONF_DEFAULT_SECURITY_ENABLED false. Because unauthenticated publish acceptance already existed in 33c58618, 75f26076 is not the smallest BIC.

Version membership: `git describe --tags --contains 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` returns `v0.1.0~18`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds for the BIC against v4.0-r4 (2573a25101514f0e3d152b96cd33b31bd00e136d, release v4.0.268), v5.0-r3 (313913737f13f97d9816dbc3d729e7bcd454a531, v5.0.213), and validated-clone HEAD b0d775a316046d4dd1ed87c0f0a9871c614f56f8.

No patch boundary exists in the validated history: at v4.0-r4, v5.0-r3, and HEAD, trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp still immediately returns success when security is disabled, while trunk/src/app/srs_app_config.cpp still sets the security default to false. The advisory reference https://github.com/ossrs/srs/releases/tag/v5.0-r3 points to v5.0.213 but that release preserves the bypass; the reporter likewise explicitly says 5.0.213 is vulnerable. Therefore neither v5.0-r3 nor any later commit through HEAD is a fix, and fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are justified nulls.

Current attack path: trunk/src/app/srs_app_rtmp_conn.cpp identifies the remote client and stream, calls security_->check, and then starts FMLE/Flash publishing. With the default-false configuration, trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp returns success before evaluating any rules, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach start_fmle_publish and receive NetStream.Publish.Start unless a deployment adds an independent control.
reasoning: The first-party-referenced technical report narrows the issue to missing mandatory authorization on RTMP publish, not the advisory summary's unsupported arbitrary-code-execution wording. History was therefore followed from the accepting NetStream.Publish.Start path rather than from later refactors. The smallest source commit that first accepts the final publish command is 33c58618: its parent can negotiate preliminary FMLE commands and create a stream but cannot consume/accept publish or emit Publish.Start. Later commit 75f26076 merely added an opt-in guard whose disabled branch retained the pre-existing allow behavior, so selecting it would mistake a later security refactor for the BIC. The BIC predates the first tagged release and is an ancestor of both reporter-tested 4.0.268 and 5.0.213. Direct inspection of those tags and current HEAD confirms the default-false allow path remains, so the repository supplies no fix SHA and the claimed `<v5.0.213` boundary is not supported by code history. Finally, AI attribution is based only on the 33c58618 commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, yielding NOT_AI independently of later AI-labeled SRS commits.
remaining_gap: Upstream remains unpatched through validated-clone HEAD b0d775a316046d4dd1ed87c0f0a9871c614f56f8: no commit changes RTMP publish to require authentication by default, so there is no fix SHA or patched version boundary. The advisory phrase `<v5.0.213` conflicts with both the v5.0-r3 tree and the reporter's explicit vulnerable result for 5.0.213; resolving that publication error would require an upstream/advisory correction, not additional repository history mining.
